answer_1.quote: Automated Essay Scoring (AES) has evolved rapidly—from linear regressors built on handcrafted features, through CNN-LSTM hybrids that capture local and long-range coherence, to transformer encoders such as R2BERT that pair BERT representations with joint regression-ranking objectives and reach state-of-the-art agreement on ASAP essays.
answer_1.outputs: The models output a single score for each essay, either on an 11-point scale (ASAP) or as one of three bands (low/medium/high for TOEFL11 and FCE).

answer_2.quote: We report conventional accuracy and QWK together with three uncertainty-aware measures introduced in Section 2: Coverage, the empirical proportion of essays whose true label lies in the prediction set; Average set size, a proxy for informativeness; and UAcc, which trades off accuracy against set size.

answer_4.quote: Quadratic-weighted κ (QWK) measures agreement with human raters while penalising larger score discrepancies more heavily than near misses, which is natural for ordinal rubrics.
answer_4.guideline: The metric penalises larger score discrepancies more heavily than near misses, which is natural for ordinal rubrics.
